## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahākassapa Sutta* (Ud 1.6) is the sixth discourse of the first chapter (Bodhivagga) of the *Udāna* [Holt et al. 2003]. The discourse recounts how the Venerable Mahākassapa, having just recovered from an extended illness, sets out on an alms-seeking round [Holt et al. 2003]. Although various deities (*deva*s) attempt to present him with food offerings, Mahākassapa turns down their gifts and deliberately chooses to seek alms among the poor and destitute instead [Holt et al. 2003]. In modern scholarship, this narrative has been analyzed alongside a closely related alms expedition later in the collection (Ud 3.7, *Sakkudāna Sutta*), drawing an analogy between emerging from prolonged illness and emerging from a seven-day meditative absorption (*samādhi*) [Holt et al. 2003]. The narrative background is further developed in Dhammapāla's *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* [Holt et al. 2003].
